titre: Enrolling my child in the school canteen and after-school care
resume: Who runs the canteen in primary school, middle school and high school, the documents to prepare to get the right rate, and where to ask for help if the cost is a problem.
aQuoiCaSert: The canteen and périscolaire (before- and after-school care, supervised homework, activities) mean your child is looked after around school hours. In nursery and primary school, the town (commune) runs them and sets the prices, often based on your family quotient (quotient familial, a family income index calculated by the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office)): without a quotient certificate, you may pay the highest rate. In middle and high school (collège and lycée), you enroll for school lunches (demi-pension) with the school itself.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of children in nursery or primary school.
Parents of middle and high school students, for school lunches (demi-pension).
Parents of a child with an allergy or on a special diet for health reasons.
aSavoir: In primary school, the town is not required to set up a canteen. But where one exists, every child enrolled at the school has the right to use it. Restricting access to children whose parents work is illegal.

Prices are set by the town for primary school, by the department for middle schools (collèges) and by the region for high schools (lycées). In Martinique, the Collectivité territoriale de Martinique (CTM, the territorial authority) holds both of these powers. Prices may take the family quotient into account.
In middle and high school, the canteen social fund (fonds social pour les cantines) can help families. It is granted by the head of the school, who sets out the conditions at the start of the year.

Allergy or diet for health reasons: an individual care plan (PAI, projet d'accueil individualisé) can be set up with the doctor. You can also provide a packed lunch, for which you are then responsible.

Separated parents: enrolling in the canteen is part of the child's everyday life. If you have shared residence, ask the town hall (mairie) whether each parent can be billed for their own weeks, and with which family quotient.

Often required for the canteen and after-school care. Ask your home or school insurer.

documents.detail: Copy, often requested for after-school care.

If you choose automatic direct debit.

etapes.detail: In primary school, ask the town hall's school or after-school service. In middle and high school, ask the school office or the bursar's office (intendance). Ask for the enrollment dates, the list of documents and the price list.
Family quotient certificate on caf.fr, tax notice on impots.gouv.fr, insurance certificate from your insurer.

Family quotient certificate, proof of address, ID, family record book, insurance certificate, vaccination pages, PAI if needed, judgment if separated, RIB for direct debit. Note which days your child will attend.
At the counter or on the town's family portal (portail famille) if there is one. Specify the canteen and after-school care days.
In primary school, ask at the town hall or the school social worker. In middle and high school, contact the social worker or the school office about the canteen social fund.
Log each payment in your Journal to keep a history of your child's expenses and make sharing costs with the other parent easier.
